title: Preserve and test the V1 secrets compatibility boundary
body:
## Outcome
Preserve the shipped `fleet secrets get|list` contract while typed credential work is added. Current verified code is `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:1-28,139-193,493-604` and `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs:1-19,73-79,110-173`: resolver uses broker then BWS fallback, redacts values in Debug/errors, rejects empty values, and CLI list reports broker names only.

## Deliverable and boundaries
Add characterization tests and a compatibility contract for source order, output, errors, list semantics, help/arity, exit codes and feature linking. Synthetic adapters only. Do not add writes, a live provider adapter, a new default source, provider credentials, or a database. Keep the restricted connect build free of the secrets domain.

## Acceptance and independent oracle
Exact tests prove broker-first then BWS fallback; empty legacy value remains unresolved; Debug/errors contain no fixture secret; malformed BWS list is unavailable, not absent; `list` never substitutes full BWS vault enumeration; usage/help and stdout/stderr/exit behavior remain stable. Oracle: deterministic fake sources and captured output.

## Negative tests
BWS listing timeout, malformed JSON, 403, bad ID, and empty response cannot return success or `NotFound`; `list` must not enumerate BWS; test fixture secret never appears in output/error.

## Dependencies, priority, lifecycle
No blockers. Small (S), first V1/V2 work. High / numeric urgency 450 because it protects the compatibility seam; lifecycle Ready for repo-only work.

## Current evidence and scope
Verified current paths above; no production vault access is needed. Affected boundary: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/**`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs`, focused tests.

## Failure, rollback, recovery, open decision
If characterization fails, do not change the default resolver. Additive tests/contracts can be reverted without external state. Recovery is to retain V1 behavior. Open decision: whether future typed API accepts valid empty strings; default is retain current behavior in the compatibility wrapper. No production or schedule change.

title: Define versioned typed Credential schema and compatibility parser
body:
## Outcome
Introduce a versioned logical Credential model independent of provider-native identity. Current evidence: no canonical schema exists in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` (resolver-only contract, lines 1-28, 139-193) or its `Cargo.toml:1-12`.

## Deliverable and technical boundary
Define logical UUID, mutable canonical ref, schema/policy version, class, typed kind/ordered fields, `Observed` states (present/null/absent/redacted/inaccessible/unknown), tags, relationships, attachment refs, lifecycle/provenance, provider binding and opaque native fields/revision refs. Support unknown types losslessly via versioned encrypted-envelope reference or explicit lossiness error. No provider calls, database, CLI tree, or migration of live data.

## Acceptance and oracle
Round-trip fixtures preserve schema versions, field ordering/type, exact native IDs and unknown fields. Parser distinguishes absent/null/empty/inaccessible. Redacted formatting and errors contain no known fixture secret. Unsupported future schema gets a typed error without dropping source data. Oracle: canonical fixture equality and explicit schema migration reference fixtures.

## Negative tests
Display-name/path collision does not merge logical IDs; BWS and Bitwarden Password Manager remain separate provider enum cases; unknown/unclassified object cannot auto-replicate; inaccessible field cannot be serialized as absent; attachment bytes never appear in metadata encoding.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends on SEC-01. Medium (M), V2 foundation; High / urgency 430, lifecycle Ready for synthetic fixtures. Blocks REC-01 and REC-02.

## Current evidence / safety
No canonical model, write path or `op`/`bw` adapter is in current V1. Work only in domain types/parser/tests under `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/**` or a reviewed shared crate. Synthetic data only; no provider tokens or vault reads.

## Rollback / recovery / open decisions
Keep V1 resolver types and behavior isolated; additive parser can be disabled before persistence. Unknown schema is retained/rejected, not destructively migrated. UUID encoding, exact field normalization registry and attachment storage are implementation-time decisions under review.

title: Add provider capability and scope descriptors with typed errors
body:
## Outcome
Provide a small provider seam with explicit capabilities, configured scopes, atomicity and typed outcomes. Current V1 hardcodes broker/BWS and has no capability descriptors or write surface (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:139-193,493-604`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Define descriptors for supported/unsupported/unknown/not-authorized operations and fields; provider/version/scope evidence; pagination, size, native revision, CAS, attachments, auth scope and consistency. Define inventory/read/create/update adapter contracts, `RevisionGuard` (CAS, preflight-and-verify with race disclosed, or unsupported), redacted errors and structured per-provider receipts. Implement fake providers only. BWS, `bw`, OP are distinct identities; no ambient authorization.

## Acceptance and oracle
Fake adapters exercise each capability state; unknown/unsupported is never success; typed `403` is `PermissionDenied`, not not-found; truncated/malformed list is incomplete; revision guard exposes non-atomic path. Receipt differentiates accepted, pending and readback-verified. Oracle: scripted fake responses and exact result-state assertions.

## Negative tests
BWS auth cannot construct `bw`; forbidden container cannot be read/written; missing attachment/field prevents “fully synced”; provider error detail and raw stdout/token are redacted; no generic delete method is callable in routine reconcile.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-01/02; blocks SEC-04/05/06 and REC-03. Medium (M), V2, High / urgency 420. Backlog until model interface is settled.

## Current evidence / safe boundary
Current crate is a read-only resolver and `fleet secrets` exposes only `get|list`. Affected seam in `fleet-secrets`; all tests synthetic; no provider access or writes.

## Rollback / recovery / open decisions
Leave V1 default chain untouched and make new seam opt-in. On capability uncertainty fail closed and keep prior checkpoint. Exact SDK/API choice and per-provider auth mechanism await current official documentation and isolated tests.

title: Implement BWS read adapter against explicit project scope
body:
## Outcome
Add explicit-scope BWS adapter while preserving existing machine-secret value and native ID semantics. Verified baseline currently invokes `bws secret list` then `bws secret get <id>` in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:517-604`; broker also lists then fetches items (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs:190-266`). This is not `bw` access.

## Deliverable and boundary
Implement read/inventory for one configured BWS project/machine identity; report granted scope/completeness and preserve native IDs, value, note/metadata and revision evidence. Choose official Rust SDK only after current API/MSRV/lockfile compatibility is verified; CLI adapter must not pass secrets via argv or log stderr. No production inventory, no write path in this issue.

## Acceptance and oracle
Synthetic or expressly isolated test-project reads show list/get agreement and stable ID; pagination/scope status explicit; redacted errors/logs; auth scope validated. Oracle: deterministic provider fixtures plus authorized isolated test project only if separately approved.

## Negative tests
Timeout, 401/403, rate limit, malformed/truncated page, bad native ID and missing item are not deletion; secret values/tokens absent from logs; scope cannot expand from configured project.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-03. Medium (M), V2, Standard / urgency 350; Backlog pending a scoped test environment.

## Failure / rollback / recovery / open decision
Keep current fallback as default until behavior parity and benchmark evidence. If an outcome is ambiguous, reread by stable native ID before retry. Exact SDK vs CLI and capability guarantees remain open pending official docs and test. Production writes remain out of scope.

title: Implement 1Password adapter for an explicit authorized vault set
body:
## Outcome
Add a structured 1Password adapter for a declared, approved vault set; an API existing in documentation is not evidence that this deployment or vault is available. Intake note `note.md:32-39` confirms no Fleet OP adapter.

## Deliverable and boundary
Start with list/read for a configured vault; then guarded create/update only where capability proven. Preserve native item UUID, category, sections, field IDs/types/order/visibility, tags, URLs, attachments and unknown data. Use full-object merge or a narrowly scoped patch; report any lossiness. CLI/API/Connect choice must be evidenced against current official docs and granted test scope. No personal vault census or production writes.

## Acceptance and oracle
Synthetic or separately approved test-vault fixture round-trips all supported fields and stable native ID; exact vault scope report; token not in argv/logs; readback proves field fidelity. Oracle: canonical fixtures and a dedicated authorized test vault when approved.

## Negative tests
403, lost vault permission, inaccessible attachment, unsupported custom field, title collision and rate limit produce typed status/conflict, never overwrite another vault or mark full sync.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02/03. Large (L), V2, Standard / urgency 340; Backlog pending service-account grant and test vault.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Feature remains optional; V1 resolver unchanged. Ambiguous write requires lookup/readback by native ID before retry. Exact CLI/API/Connect transport and grants are open; no authorization inferred.

title: Specify separately authorized Bitwarden Password Manager adapter
stage: V2 later authorized source / Sweep B
body:
## Outcome
Define distinct adapter/auth/scope boundaries for Bitwarden Password Manager (`bw`) rich login records and a separately authorized Sweep B. Current intake `note.md:34-50` says `bw` is not authorized; current Fleet code only contains BWS (`fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:493-604`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Research current first-party CLI/API behavior for login categories, URI match rules, folders/collections, custom typed fields, TOTP/passkey limitations, attachments, unlock/session and replace semantics. Propose native-fidelity adapter contract and exact scope/report requirements. Synthetic serialization fixtures allowed. No personal-vault login, export, access, migration or inventory.

## Acceptance and oracle
Document distinct provider enum/config/auth/token type; capability matrix cites primary docs and versions; fixture proves rich-field shape and replacement hazard; explicit access approval and grant checklist precede implementation. Oracle: source-cited doc matrix plus fixtures.

## Negative tests
BWS token/config cannot instantiate `bw`; no automatic session discovery; no inventory without explicit scope approval; unreadable passkey/OTP is inaccessible/unsupported, not absent; reduced projection cannot replace full native item.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02/03. Medium (M), V2 later, Standard / urgency 260; Blocked for real access and migration; design/research may proceed.

## Rollback / recovery / open decisions
No enabled code path; no migration to roll back. Reassess when access is explicitly authorized. Open: authorized account/vault set, API/export limits and native field fidelity.

title: Define root escrow policy separate from generic credential replication
body:
## Outcome
Model addendum's three explicit root escrow destinations separately from generic replication: encrypted local laptop storage, approved BWS project, approved 1Password vault. Current design-pass approval explicitly forbids production root generation/export/upload (`note.md:26-30`).

## Deliverable and boundaries
Define `RootEscrowPolicy` with three independently named scope entries, encryption/recovery recipients, access controls, integrity manifests, destination-specific write/readback/restore receipts, active signer vs escrow role, and no signer auto-discovery. R2 may be separately researched, never default destination. Do not auto-expand to all future providers. Synthetic key fixtures only; no production key operations.

## Acceptance and oracle
Policy validation rejects wildcard/all-provider destinations and incomplete declared three-destination policy. Each synthetic archive can be independently restored and matches its fixture public identity. One unavailable target yields incomplete custody, not success. No signer is inferred from public certificate. Recovery key cannot be stored only inside the archive it decrypts. Oracle: policy validator and independent restoration test.

## Negative tests
`ca-root` denied under generic sync/cache; no production generation/read/export/write; a missing destination blocks “complete”; failed restoration blocks completion; root scope cannot inherit V4 federation.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02/03; coordinate with #9163, do not absorb PKI implementation. Medium (M), V2/V3 seam; High / urgency 440. Blocked for production operations; synthetic schema tests can proceed.

## Rollback / recovery / open decisions
Keep feature disabled; never delete existing escrow copies as compensation. Before activation require separate approval, reviewed crypto format, independent recovery channels and tested restore. Exact format, recovery custody and active-signer workflow remain open.

title: Define class-aware resolution and cache freshness contract
body:
## Outcome
Define policy-aware freshness, source provenance, cache invalidation and offline behavior. Current broker retains previous per-secret values after failed refresh and serves cache age (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs:244-266,280-346,532-545`); intake reports stale-after-rotation defect #6767. This is a known defect, not a claim of policy compliance.

## Deliverable and boundary
Specify live/memory/encrypted snapshot modes, class-specific max age, revision/provenance, revocation, write invalidation and stale result statuses. Default deny stale/offline `ca-root`, recovery, transient and revoked/unknown credentials. Stale reads never authorize writes or overwrite sources. Implement synthetic tests and a bounded V1 #6767 fix; no production store or scheduler changes.

## Acceptance and oracle
Successful rotation invalidates exact cache binding or makes freshness-required read fail; failed refresh does not reset age; allowed stale result reports source/revision/age/reason; divergent replica cannot be fallback; no cache write authority. Oracle: fake clock/provider and cache-state assertions.

## Negative tests
Old token never served for a freshness-required class; outage does not make stale value look fresh; revoked marker blocks snapshot; unknown age is not fresh; root/recovery/transient offline read denied.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-03; isolated #6767 repair may proceed alongside. Medium (M), V1/V2 bridge, High / urgency 430; Backlog. Numeric TTLs require measured benchmarks and class policy.

## Rollback / recovery / open decisions
Rollback to live-only fail-closed reads. Recover via authoritative provider read and exact cache eviction, never cached writeback. TTL/max-age and revocation propagation targets remain open; do not invent values.

title: Implement typed inventory completeness and protected baseline records
body:
## Outcome
Represent exact scope inventory quality and protect last verified common baseline. Current V1 distinguishes malformed BWS list from absence (`fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:554-604`) but has no cross-provider inventory or baseline; broker list handling is not reconciliation delete proof.

## Deliverable and boundary
Implement `Complete|Incomplete|Inaccessible|ScopeChanged|Unsupported` inventory result with pagination/cursor/scope/filter/field accessibility evidence. Add encrypted local baseline artifact and metadata checkpoint referencing exact scope, policy/schema/mapping versions and manifest hash. Synthetic adapters only; no real inventory, database deployment or secret values in plaintext journal.

## Acceptance and oracle
Complete only when every required page and field is observed for exact declared scope. Incomplete run cannot advance common watermark. Baseline round-trips protected, metadata redacted, prior checkpoint remains authoritative. Oracle: generated inventory/page fixtures and independent completeness predicate.

## Negative tests
Timeout, 403, truncated page, malformed record, scope shrink, inaccessible attachment, cursor reset never yields deletion or Complete; no secret plaintext in journal/index.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02/03; blocks REC-02 and REC-06. Medium (M), V3 first, High / urgency 450; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
No live baseline migration. Ignore unreferenced temp artifacts, retain prior checkpoint, retry incomplete observation. Select artifact atomic-write/fsync mechanism for target laptop and document its guarantee before production.

title: Build pure three-way field planner and conflict records
body:
## Outcome
Implement deterministic planner `(baseline,left,right,policy,mapping) -> Plan` with typed per-field changes and durable conflicts. Current `fleet secrets` has only get/list and no reconciliation (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs:1-19,73-79`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Pure logic only: no provider call or mutation. Use stable native refs/revisions, explicit matching evidence, typed unknown/inaccessible/null/absent/empty values and mapping-version compatibility. Timestamp never decides protected-field winner.

## Acceptance and oracle
Model-based generated scenarios compare output to an independent reference merge model: unchanged→no-op; one-sided change→only unchanged peer candidate; disjoint changes merge; same-value concurrent changes converge; divergent protected changes conflict and preserve both. Unknown/inaccessible never deletes; title-only never pairs. Oracle is reference function over generated state.

## Negative tests
Skewed clocks with two password changes still conflict; null vs absent vs empty remain distinct; unmapped custom field blocks “fully synced”; mapping mismatch fails closed; attachment inaccessible cannot be considered equal.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02 and REC-01. Medium (M), V3; High / urgency 440; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Pure planner has no side effects and can be disabled; re-plan from prior checkpoint and fresh complete inventories. Any non-secret metadata auto-merge whitelist remains a reviewed explicit choice.

title: Add revision guards, idempotency ledger, and operation receipts
body:
## Outcome
Make guarded operations and uncertain writes recoverable without claiming provider CAS/idempotency that is not documented. Current `fleet-secrets` is read-only (`Cargo.toml:9-12`, `src/lib.rs:139-193`).

## Deliverable and boundary
WAL records exact native refs/revisions, deterministic operation/idempotency identity, guard kind (`CAS`, `preflight_then_verify` with race disclosed, unsupported), provider receipt, readback state and recovery action. Fake providers only.

## Acceptance and oracle
Stale expected revision becomes precondition conflict; repeated same idempotency key maps to one logical operation in fake adapter; lost response becomes `unknown_outcome`; accepted/pending/readback-verified are distinct; no pair atomicity claim. Oracle: fake provider with deterministic revision/receipt model.

## Negative tests
Never blind-retry create after lost response if lookup is unavailable; concurrent revision change stops operation; zero exit with contradictory response is not success; non-CAS adapter clearly exposes race.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-03 and REC-02; precedes REC-05/07. Medium (M), V3, High / urgency 430; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Do not expose mutation until contract is accepted. Replay first reconciles provider by stable ID/marker. Exact per-provider CAS/idempotency semantics remain source-verification requirements, not assumptions. No production adapter access in this task.

title: Persist append-only local journal and metadata-only outbox
body:
## Outcome
Create a durable local event journal and replayable metadata-only remote outbox. Current repo has general queue/outbox patterns but no secrets journal; secrets V1 explicitly persists no secret value (`fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:15-28`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Append/fsync immutable schema-versioned events before effects; integrity chain, sequence and redaction class; outbox dedup by event ID and sink with receipt. SQL projection is secondary and contains metadata only. Fake sink, local fixtures; no production DB deployment or live inventory.

## Acceptance and oracle
Replayed duplicate deliveries are idempotent; event history never mutates; interrupted append detected and recovery is explicit; chain verifies; remote sink outage never means committed; journal write failure prevents external effect. Scan every output for fixture secrets, tokens, unkeyed low-entropy hashes; assert absent. Oracle: replay reference and redaction scanner.

## Negative tests
Malformed/corrupt event blocks replay; SQL ack cannot advance provider baseline; item paths/IDs are not metric labels; no plaintext secret or token reaches journal/index/log.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02 and REC-01; needed by REC-05/07. Medium (M), V3, High / urgency 440; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Disable remote projection but preserve local journal. Restore/index rebuild replays immutable events. Hash chain does not prove signer identity; separately decide if signatures are needed and define signing-key custody before adding them.

title: Implement protected zz.delete history lifecycle and in-place update saga
stage: V3 synthetic saga; production use approval-blocked
body:
## Outcome
Preserve old value as protected dated `zz.delete` history in explicitly approved replicas, then update original stale active native item in place. No V1 write/reconcile exists; the mandatory algorithm is specified in `fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md:1154-1162`. Current handoff prohibits live writes (`note.md:26-30`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Implement synthetic state-machine saga: preconditions; durable history intent; idempotent history create; readback; guarded active update by exact existing native ID; verify typed fields/URLs/autofill; append event. Tombstone reasons distinguish retired, deleted-on-source, moved, revoked, compromised, inaccessible, unknown. Normal reconcile has no physical delete.

## Acceptance and oracle
Synthetic providers prove stable native item ID and login metadata; all required history copies verify before update; partial history failure blocks update; crash/retry does not duplicate history; active update failure leaves recoverable partial state; history never auto-purged. Oracle: saga reference state machine plus fake-store readback.

## Negative tests
No title-match overwrite; no timestamp winner; no physical delete call; inaccessible required history blocks active update; unavailable old value yields unrecoverable tombstone without fabricated secret; no live store/key access in this task.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-02/03/07 and REC-02/03/04; High / urgency 450, Large (L), V3. Blocked for production use, synthetic work may proceed.

## Rollback / recovery / approval
Never delete history as rollback; corrective operation is a new reviewed forward event. Resume by persisted step and reread. Production `zz.delete`, live rotation, full inventory and personal vault changes require explicit applicable approval, exact reviewed plan and recovery controls. Retention/access roles remain operator decision; no automatic purge.

title: Add authoritative deletion-candidate confirmation and scope-move handling
body:
## Outcome
Permit deletion classification only after complete same-scope evidence and confirmation. Existing BWS resolver treats malformed list as unavailable, not absent (`fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:560-585`); no cross-provider deletion engine exists.

## Deliverable and boundary
Pure candidate state machine uses prior verified native binding, complete current inventory, pagination/scope proof, movement check and second authoritative scan or verified provider event. Distinguish missing, moved, scope removed, revoked, inaccessible and unknown. It plans tombstone/history only; it does not physically delete.

## Acceptance and oracle
Model-based generated observations compare against candidate-state reference model. Before confirmation status remains `missing_candidate`; after sufficient evidence a tombstone plan is allowed only; move preserves logical ID. Oracle: explicit state transition model.

## Negative tests
Timeout, 403, rate limit, partial page, malformed response, cursor reset, narrower scope, outage and inaccessible attachment never mean deleted; reappearance is resurrection/new-generation conflict, not silent restoration.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends REC-01/02 and SEC-03. Medium (M), V3, High / urgency 430; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Disable deletion classification and retain `unknown`; recover through complete authorized full scan plus review. A provider-native deletion feed can substitute for second scan only after version-specific semantics are verified. No live inventory without approval.

title: Add guarded apply, crash injection, and resumable item saga
body:
## Outcome
Apply only an immutable approved plan and recover safely at every crash boundary. Current implementation has no write/reconcile surface; source spec requires item-level saga, receipts and no cross-provider atomicity (`§§20.2-20.5`, `21.4`).

## Deliverable and boundary
Approval is bound to plan digest, exact scope, expiry and max changes. Durable operation journal precedes external effect; bounded concurrency and rate-limit-aware retry; unknown outcomes reconciled before retry; verification precedes checkpoint. Synthetic providers and crash injection only.

## Acceptance and oracle
Inject crash before/after intent, accepted request with lost reply, partial history, active update/readback failure, journal/outbox/baseline commit. After resume, fake provider state and journal match reference saga model; no duplicate history, stale overwrite, false success or watermark advance. Changed revisions invalidate approval. Oracle: model-based crash-state oracle.

## Negative tests
`force` cannot bypass policy; non-idempotent unknown result is not retried blindly; required peer failure prevents completed run; no cross-store atomic claim; incomplete inventory does not checkpoint.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends REC-01..06 and SEC-03/07. Large (L), V3, High / urgency 440; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Feature-flag apply off until gates pass. Recovery is forward-only, with per-operation committed effect and next action. No physical delete compensation. Confirm target laptop fsync/atomic rename and lock properties before production. No live operations in this issue.

title: Define full-scan versus incremental scheduling and checkpoint policy
stage: V3 operations after safe first-run cutover
body:
## Outcome
Provide reliable laptop daily execution only after safe initial migration and approved plan, with full scans periodically and incremental cursors as hints. Current repository has no secrets reconciliation schedule in V1. Root `AGENTS.md` requires the unified fleet schedule registry be updated in the same pass as any schedule change.

## Deliverable and boundary
Reusable CLI/library run contract, exact scope lock, persistent restart-after-sleep behavior, bounded retry, last-complete watermark and full-scan cadence. Timer invokes library; choose existing control plane/systemd only after repo conventions. No live schedule enablement in design pass.

## Acceptance and oracle
Synthetic restart/resume retains last complete baseline; invalid cursor triggers full inventory; overlapping run prevented; stale lease does not take over unknown operation; tests never access real secrets. Oracle: scheduler/fake executor state assertions.

## Negative tests
Incomplete run cannot advance watermark; cursor-only absence cannot delete; no production timer before reviewed first-run migration, restore test and explicit approval.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends REC-01/07 and coordinate #9165. Medium (M), late V3, Standard / urgency 360; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Disable timer, retain checkpoints/journal, run plan-only full scan when authorized. Daily time and schedule owner remain implementation/ops decision; update registry if actual schedule is created or changed.

title: Define cache and revocation coupling for reconciled writes and replicas
stage: V1 cache correction / V3 policy integration
body:
## Outcome
Prevent broker/cache/replica stale values from surviving verified rotation or revocation under a freshness-required policy. Current broker retains old values for failed fetches and reports age (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs:244-266,280-346,532-545`); issue #6767 is cited in intake.

## Deliverable and boundary
Invalidate or refresh exact logical/native cache binding after a verified write; expose stale/age/revision/source status; class-specific max age and encrypted offline snapshot gates. No cache can authorize writes. Synthetic provider/cache tests; isolated #6767 fix may be separate.

## Acceptance and oracle
Successful rotation does not return old value for freshness-required policy; failed invalidation marks stale/unknown and refuses; permitted stale read includes source, age, revision and policy reason; divergence blocks fallback; revoked marker wins over warm cache. Oracle: fake clock/cache/provider state machine.

## Negative tests
Provider outage cannot reset age; unknown age not fresh; root/recovery/transient denied offline; revoked value never returned; stale read never writes back.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends SEC-08, REC-03/07. Medium (M), V1/V3 bridge, High / urgency 420; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Fail closed/live-only if invalidation is unavailable. Recover through authoritative reread and exact eviction; never write cached content to source. Numeric TTL and max-age values require benchmark and security decision, not assumption.
